title: 1977 AHSME Problem 26
statement: Let \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c\) and \(d\) be the lengths of sides \(MN,\) \(NP,\) \(PQ\) and \(QM,\) respectively, of quadrilateral \(MNPQ.\) If \(A\) is the area of \(MNPQ,\) then

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text:
\(A=\left(\frac{a+c}{2}\right)\left(\frac{b+d}{2}\right)\) if
and only if \(MNPQ\) is convex

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
\(A=\left(\frac{a+c}{2}\right)\left(\frac{b+d}{2}\right)\) if and
only if \(MNPQ\) is a rectangle

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
\(A\le\left(\frac{a+c}{2}\right)\left(\frac{b+d}{2}\right)\) if
and only if \(MNPQ\) is a rectangle

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
\(A\le\left(\frac{a+c}{2}\right)\left(\frac{b+d}{2}\right)\) if
and only if \(MNPQ\) is a parallelogram

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
\(A\ge\left(\frac{a+c}{2}\right)\left(\frac{b+d}{2}\right)\) if
and only if \(MNPQ\) is a parallelogram

solutions.text:
Splitting along diagonal \(MP\) and using \(\sin\theta\le1\) gives \(A\le\frac{ab+cd}{2}.\) Splitting along \(NQ\) similarly gives \(A\le\frac{ad+bc}{2}.\) These bounds remain valid for a nonconvex quadrilateral by taking the appropriate difference of triangle areas. Adding them yields \[ \begin{aligned} 2A&\le\frac{ab+ad+bc+cd}{2}\\ &=\frac{(a+c)(b+d)}2, \end{aligned} \] or \(A\le\left(\frac{a+c}{2}\right)\left(\frac{b+d}{2}\right).\) Equality requires equality in all four sine bounds, so all four angles are right angles; conversely a rectangle gives equality. Thus the equality holds exactly for rectangles.

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Split the quadrilateral along each diagonal and bound every sine by \(1\)
Combine the two resulting area bounds and analyze when every bound is an equality
